audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer phases[0..6].side are all templated 'Skill' with generic why text, while content win[0..6] already carries the real per-stage winner (Galio/Alistar/Alistar/Alistar/Galio/Alistar/Alistar) backed by concrete whys[]. The two layers disagree, so the page would show a flat 'Skill' chart against a decisive content narrative.
audit.why: Alistar has no knockup pre-6 minus his combo, giving Galio the level-1 poke trade, but his W-Q Headbutt-Pulverize (14-10s CD) takes over at 2 and holds priority through items until Hero's Entrance comes online at 6 and swings it back.
audit.corrected: Set phases[N].side to match win[N] for all 7 stages and rewrite phases[N].why to state the actual reason (grounded in the same facts as whys[N]) instead of the generic template text.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns names Headbutt as matchup-defining but contains no cooldown number, and dosFull[1]/dontsFull[2] were pasted verbatim from tradeGood/tradeBad under unrelated titles instead of describing the actual cooldown window.
audit.why: Alistar's Pulverize (Q, 14-10s) and Headbutt (W, 14-10s) share a curve so the combo resets together; Unbreakable Will (R) is 120/100/80s, meaning an early spent R is a long punishable window.
audit.corrected: Rewrite breakdown.cooldowns with real numbers, and replace the two copy-pasted bullets with text that actually matches their titles.

audit.whatIsWrong: The auto-reset tell on Trample (E) — his combo opens with an auto-attack reset, and the wind-up is the readable cue — is not stated anywhere in the full layer.
audit.why: missingInteractions flags this as applicable and absent; Trample's flags include autoReset ('auto-attack reset — burst timing tell').
audit.corrected: Add a new Do's entry naming the Trample wind-up as the step-back cue.

edits.before: Q the pair — the tornado tick chips duos that stand in formation.
edits.after: Alistar has no knockup until level 2, so Winds of War poke and your bigger frame win the opening trade.

edits.before: W charge threat begins: the taunt governs their engage plans already.
edits.after: His level-2 W-Q pancake plus Flash can delete your ADC before you react — the scariest spike in the lane.

edits.before: Full kit: E-W the committed trade and the magic shield refunds their poke.
edits.after: His combo still out-CCs Justice Punch and punishes any forward step you take.

edits.before: Zone with taunt threat and shield the margins — AP duos pay double rent.
edits.after: He keeps combo priority and threatens the all-in whenever your E is down.

edits.before: Hero's Entrance online — every roam your duo survives, you end.
edits.after: Hero's Entrance lets you counter-engage or reset his dives, swinging the fight to you.

edits.before: First item: the taunt rotation chunks and the MR makes mage supports cry.
edits.after: With his mythic and R online his combo becomes near-unkillable, retaking the trade edge.

edits.before: Late Galio is the anti-dive: taunt their engage off your carry and R the map's emergencies.
edits.after: His relentless peel and engage outscale your single flip in the extended 2v2.

edits.before: - Alistar Headbutt: matchup-defining — The headbutt-pulverize combo starts every play — respect flash range while it is up. Read it before every duo step-up. - Your W Shield of Durand answers exactly one disaster per cooldown. - Spend the R on swing moments only.
edits.after: - Alistar's Headbutt (W) is 14s early, down to 10s at max, matching Pulverize (Q)'s curve — the combo resets together. Respect flash range while it's up. - Your W Shield of Durand (18-14s) answers one disaster per cycle. - Save the 180/160/140s R for swing moments only.

edits.before: Bait the answer, start the chain, and let your carry collect — engage trades are all-or-nothing; pick the all.
edits.after: Once his 14-10s Headbutt-Pulverize combo is spent, the window is yours — dash in with Justice Punch before it resets.

edits.before: Engaging into a banked disengage — the chain that starts answered is a donation with armor.
edits.after: He can flash-cancel your engage into his own Headbutt — trading his flash window evenly hands him the reset, not you.
Alistar's combo opens with an auto-attack reset off Trample (E) — the wind-up is your cue to step back, not the cast itself.
